title: Mean and median show different centres
summary: The mean adds values and divides by their count. The median is the middle value after sorting. A very large value can pull the mean upward.
introduction: The mean adds values and divides by their count. The median is the middle value after sorting. A very large value can pull the mean upward. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain mean and median show different centres
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: The mean adds values and divides by their count. The median is the middle value after sorting. A very large value can pull the mean upward.

blocks.code:
from statistics import mean, median
minutes = [2, 3, 4, 5, 36]
print(mean(minutes), median(minutes))
blocks.title: Mean and median show different centres

blocks.text: The output is 10 4. The sum is 50 across five values. The middle sorted value is 4. The value 36 pulls the mean far above the median.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Replace 36 with 6 and compare both measures.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not report an average without checking how spread out the values are.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).
